commentary.text:
I’m claiming a central square immediately, establishing a durable foothold while keeping Red’s remaining formation flexible for later sandwiches and support of Yellow’s center approach.
```memo
### Position read
Opening position. We placed Red on (3,3), securing one center square without triggering a capture. Losses remain 0–0–0–0.

### Our plan
Contest all four center squares with both colors while preserving rook lanes. Use the advanced Red as an anchor for future same-color sandwiches; watch for opponent pieces entering its row or column. Yellow should seek a complementary center foothold unless a concrete capture or defensive necessity appears.

### Opponent tendencies
No opponent move has occurred yet.

### Lessons
Moving into a sandwich is safe; captures trigger only from the mover’s landing square and require matching-color flankers. Teammates cannot complete sandwiches and can be friendly-fire casualties.
```

I’m claiming the safe central square at (4,4). Unlike (3,4), it cannot be immediately sandwiched against Red’s piece at (3,3), and it blocks Yellow’s direct route into (3,4).
```memo
### Position read
Red opened from (0,3) to center (3,3). We answered with Blue from (4,7) to (4,4), safely occupying a diagonal center square. Losses remain 0-0-0-0.
### Our plan
Hold (4,4), contest every center entry, and develop same-color flank geometry. Expect Yellow may take (4,3); if so, avoid forcing friendly-fire captures and look for a safe way to dislodge it. Red at (3,3) makes Blue moves onto (3,2) or (3,4) vulnerable to a future Red sandwich.
### Opponent tendencies
The opponent immediately advanced Red into the center, suggesting an aggressive center-occupation plan.
### Lessons
Before every move, test all four landing-square rays for mixed-color sandwiches and adjacent groups for enclosure. Same-color flanks are mandatory; teammate pieces can be captured as part of a line.
```

Yellow takes a central foothold beside Red, denying Green access to (4,3) and creating a potential horizontal sandwich against Blue’s piece on (4,4).
```memo
### Position read
Red occupies (3,3), Blue occupies (4,4), and Yellow now occupies (4,3); all losses remain zero. The remaining center square (3,4) is open and currently reachable by Red from (0,4). Yellow on (4,3) is safe from an immediate Green sandwich.

### Our plan
Red should consider (0,4)→(3,4) unless Green creates a stronger tactical need. Blue on (4,4) is threatened by a future Yellow landing on (4,5), using Yellow (4,3) as the far flanker; expect Blue to move or disrupt that formation. Seek occupation of the last center and then remove or displace Blue from (4,4).

### Opponent tendencies
Blue answered our first center move by occupying the diagonally opposite center, indicating direct center contest.

### Lessons
Central anchors can create sandwich threats across neighboring center squares. Always check whether the opponent can vacate the threatened piece before investing another move in the setup.
```

I’m placing Green beneath Yellow’s central piece to build a same-color vertical capture frame. If Red vacates (3,3), Green can threaten to land there and sandwich Yellow against this new flank.
```memo
### Position read
We hold Blue at (4,4); the opponent holds Red (3,3) and Yellow (4,3). Green moved (5,0)→(5,3), creating a potential vertical sandwich on Yellow if Green can later land at (3,3). Losses remain 0-0-0-0.
### Our plan
If Red vacates (3,3), threaten Green (3,0)→(3,3), which would capture Yellow at (4,3) against Green (5,3). Protect Blue (4,4): Yellow can capture it next turn with (7,5)→(4,5), using Yellow (4,3) as the far flank. On Blue’s turn, either move the exposed Blue or block that route, potentially with Blue (5,7)→(5,5), after checking Red’s move.
### Opponent tendencies
The opponent is aggressively occupying the center with both colors and has an immediate sandwich geometry against our central Blue.
### Lessons
Track landing-square capture triggers only. Same-color stationary flanks enable sandwiches; entering a sandwich is safe, but leaving a piece exposed to an opponent landing before its next move is not.
```

I’m taking the remaining open central square with Red, consolidating three of the four center points while preserving Yellow’s potential sandwich against the Blue piece at (4,4).
```memo
### Position read
We occupy (3,3), (3,4), and (4,3); the opponent occupies (4,4). Green has advanced to (5,3), directly below our Yellow center piece. All loss counts remain zero.

### Our plan
Preserve the three-square center formation. Yellow can capture Blue on (4,4) by landing at (4,5), using Yellow (4,3) as the far flanker, if Blue remains there and the route stays open. After clearing (4,4), aim to occupy it for immediate center victory. Watch for attacks on our central anchors.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent contests the center directly with Blue and has moved Green toward the underside of our Yellow anchor, suggesting disruption or containment.

### Lessons
A center capture only clears the final square; a later occupation is still needed to win. Recheck all four landing-square capture rays and adjacent enclosure groups before every move.
```

I’m blocking Yellow’s route to (4,5), preventing the sandwich capture of our Blue center piece while keeping our hold on (4,4).
```memo
### Position read
We hold Blue at (4,4), while the opponent holds Red at (3,3),(3,4) and Yellow at (4,3). Blue moved (5,7)→(5,5), blocking Yellow’s path from (7,5) to (4,5), which had threatened to sandwich our center Blue against Yellow (4,3). Green remains at (5,3). Losses are 0-0-0-0.
### Our plan
Preserve (4,4) and prevent the opponent from consolidating all four center squares. Green still has useful same-color geometry: if (3,3) becomes empty, Green may land there from (3,0), sandwiching Yellow (4,3) against Green (5,3). Look for Blue support near the center and captures against the two adjacent Reds.
### Opponent tendencies
The opponent is aggressively occupying three center squares and building same-color sandwich threats against our lone central piece.
### Lessons
A blocker anywhere on an opponent’s rook path can deny a dangerous landing. Recheck whether the blocker itself creates a new sandwich line before committing.
```

Blue’s move to (5,5) blocks the direct Yellow route to (4,5), so I’m repositioning another Yellow piece to (4,6). This renews the sandwich threat against Blue on (4,4): Yellow can land on (4,5), capture the center blocker using (4,3) as the far flank, and then Red can occupy the cleared center.
```memo
### Position read
We hold three center squares: Red at (3,3),(3,4) and Yellow at (4,3). Blue blocks the fourth at (4,4). Blue (5,5) prevented the original Yellow route to (4,5), so Yellow has repositioned from (7,6) to (4,6). Green remains at (5,3). Losses are all zero.

### Our plan
Yellow now threatens (4,6)→(4,5), sandwiching Blue (4,4) against Yellow (4,3). After that capture, Red (3,4)→(4,4) can complete the center immediately. If Blue vacates (4,4), occupy it directly with Yellow (4,3) or Red (3,4), provided all four centers remain ours. Prioritize preserving both Red center anchors and Yellow (4,3).

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent contests the last center with Blue and used Blue (5,5) to block our first capture route. Green is positioned below our Yellow anchor and may attempt disruption.

### Lessons
Recalculate routes after every blocking move. A non-center sandwich capture must be followed by immediate center occupation; check whether Red can finish before the opponent dismantles an anchor.
```

I’m breaking the opponent’s center formation immediately. Green lands at (2,3), using our Green at (5,3) as the far flank to sandwich and capture both Red at (3,3) and Yellow at (4,3).
```memo
### Position read
Green moved (2,0)→(2,3), sandwiching and capturing Red (3,3) plus Yellow (4,3) against Green (5,3). The opponent’s three-square center formation is broken; only Red (3,4) remains in the center, alongside our Blue (4,4). Expected losses: Red 1, Yellow 1, Blue 0, Green 0.
### Our plan
Keep Blue (4,4) secure and contest the cleared center squares. Green now has a strong vertical pair at (2,3) and (5,3); watch for future lines through column 3. Seek another multi-capture against either opponent color, both now one loss closer to elimination.
### Opponent tendencies
The opponent aggressively occupies center squares and recently used Yellow (7,6)→(4,6) to approach laterally.
### Lessons
Mixed-color sandwich lines are valuable: every intervening non-moving-color piece is captured when same-color flanks close the line.
```

I’m developing Red at (2,2), creating an immediate sandwich threat against the advanced Green piece at (2,3): Red can move from (3,4) to (2,4) next turn and capture it. This pressures Green to break its dangerous vertical formation while keeping our remaining central anchor in place.
```memo
### Position read
Green’s move from (2,0) to (2,3) sandwiched and captured our Red (3,3) and Yellow (4,3), leaving us with only Red (3,4) in the center. Blue occupies (4,4). Green pieces at (2,3) and (5,3) form a dangerous vertical pair. Losses: Red 1, Yellow 1, opponent colors 0.

### Our plan
Red at (2,2) now threatens Red (3,4)→(2,4), sandwiching Green (2,3). If Green retreats, its central formation is weakened; if it stays, take the capture when tactically safe. Yellow (4,6) should seek (4,5), while another Yellow or Red develops toward (4,3) to challenge Blue (4,4). Preserve Red (3,4) unless moving it wins material or prevents a stronger threat.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent spots mixed-color sandwich tactics and used the Green pair on column 3 to erase two center occupants at once. Blue continues holding the final lower-right center.

### Lessons
Before filling an empty center, scan beyond it for same-colored opponent flanks; self-entry is safe, but our later placement can be captured by a newly moved flank. Break prepared sandwich structures before rebuilding the center.
```

I remove the opponent’s last central piece while pushing that color to two losses. The landing piece is supported from below; on our next turn, the adjacent piece at (2,3) should move vertically—ideally to (4,3)—to break the opponent’s potential horizontal sandwich and strengthen our center.
```memo
### Position read
Our move (2,7)→(2,4) captures the opponent piece at (3,4) against our (4,4), raising that opponent color to 2 losses. We retain (4,4) as the only occupied center square. Our pieces at (2,3) and (2,4) are adjacent, with an opponent piece at (2,2).
### Our plan
On our next color turn, move (2,3) vertically, preferably to center (4,3), unless the opponent creates a stronger emergency. This breaks the dangerous line where an opponent piece could land at (2,5) and sandwich both (2,4) and (2,3) against (2,2). Then seek one more capture to eliminate the opponent color already at 2 losses.
### Opponent tendencies
The opponent contests the center aggressively and has advanced an edge piece to (2,2), creating latent horizontal capture geometry.
### Lessons
After making a capture, inspect whether the landing piece and an adjacent teammate piece form a mixed-color line that an opponent can close against its own far flank.
```

I’m placing Yellow beside the central Blue piece to establish the far flank for a future Yellow move to (4,3), which would capture Blue at (4,4). This also leaves intact Red’s immediate row-2 tactic if Green does not break the mixed chain.
```memo
### Position read
We have Red at (0,1),(0,5),(0,6),(2,2) and Yellow at (4,5),(7,1),(7,2),(7,4),(7,5). The opponent holds Blue at (2,4),(4,4),(5,5) and the right edge, with Green at (2,3),(5,3) and much of the left edge. Losses: Red 2, Yellow 1, opponent colors 0. One more Red loss eliminates Red.

### Our plan
If Green (2,3) remains, Red (0,5)→(2,5) sandwiches and captures the mixed Green (2,3)+Blue (2,4) line against Red (2,2). Yellow (4,5) is now the far flank for a future Yellow landing at (4,3), which would capture Blue (4,4). Develop Yellow (7,1) toward (4,1), then (4,3), unless a faster route or defensive need appears.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent actively detects mixed-color sandwiches and attacks our center occupants. Expect Green to retreat from (2,3) and Blue to move from (4,4) once the Yellow pincer becomes immediate.

### Lessons
Red is at elimination point, so check every opponent sandwich before moving it. Use threats that force central defenders to retreat even when the capture is unlikely to be allowed.
```

I’m moving the exposed Green piece off row 2, breaking Red’s potential sandwich against our Blue piece. Placing it at (3,3) also claims a second center square and threatens to complete the center with Blue at (3,4), followed by Green at (4,3).
```memo
### Position read
We occupy center squares (3,3) with Green and (4,4) with Blue. Moving Green off (2,3) breaks the opponent’s threatened row-2 sandwich against Blue (2,4). The opponent colors have 2 and 1 losses; we have none.
### Our plan
Unless an emergency appears, next move Blue (2,4)→(3,4), creating a three-square center occupation. Then Green (5,3)→(4,3) completes all four centers and wins immediately. Verify after each opponent move that (3,4) and (4,3) remain empty and that neither central piece has become immediately capturable.
### Opponent tendencies
The opponent contests the center and builds long rook-line sandwich threats. Their color at 2 losses is one capture from elimination.
### Lessons
A center advance is strongest when it simultaneously breaks an exposed sandwich line. Check mixed-color friendly lines carefully because one enemy color can capture both.
```

Blue could otherwise play from (3,7) to (3,5), sandwiching Yellow at (4,5) against Blue at (5,5). Red occupies that landing square, preserving Yellow while developing toward the center.
```memo
### Position read
After our move, Red occupies (0,1),(0,6),(2,2),(3,5); Yellow occupies (4,5),(7,1),(7,2),(7,4),(7,5). The opponent has central pieces at Green (3,3) and Blue (4,4), plus Blue (2,4),(5,5). Losses remain: Red 2, Yellow 1, opponent colors 0. Red is one loss from elimination.

### Our plan
Red (3,5) blocks Blue (3,7)→(3,5), which would have captured Yellow (4,5) against Blue (5,5). Preserve Red carefully and use it to contest the upper center. Yellow still aims to exploit its flank at (4,5): reaching (4,3) would capture Blue (4,4), but the current piece cannot cross that blocker, so develop another Yellow via column 1 or 2.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent retreats from direct mixed-line threats and looks for sandwiches using already aligned pieces. Expect Blue to reposition the central blocker or attack Red (2,2), and Green to protect (3,3).

### Lessons
Before every move, scan opponent landing squares adjacent to our pieces; the Blue (3,7)/(5,5) alignment made defending Yellow urgent. Moving into a sandwich is safe, but leaving an opponent a legal landing that completes one is not.
```

Red’s shift to (3,5) does not stop our center plan. Blue takes (3,4), securing three central squares; Yellow cannot reach or block (4,3), so Green is poised to complete the center next turn.
```memo
### Position read
We now occupy three centers: Green (3,3), Blue (3,4), and Blue (4,4). The opponent has no legal Yellow move that can occupy (4,3), capture a central piece, or obstruct Green’s route there. Losses remain: opponent colors 2 and 1; ours 0 and 0.
### Our plan
On Green’s next turn, play (5,3)→(4,3) to complete all four central squares and win immediately. First verify Yellow’s move did not unexpectedly alter a central square or the route, though current geometry makes disruption impossible.
### Opponent tendencies
The opponent contests the center and builds rook-line sandwiches. Red’s piece at (3,5) could later combine with a landing at (3,2), but the center win should occur first.
### Lessons
When a two-move center finish is available, verify not only captures but whether the intervening color can occupy the final square or block the finishing piece’s rook path.
```

The opponent threatens to complete the four-square center immediately. I advance Yellow to (4,2), blocking the edge Green’s route to (4,3) and preparing a sandwich of the Blue piece on (4,4) against Yellow (4,5). This forces the opponent to use its remaining central route if it wants the instant win.
```memo
### Position read
We moved Yellow from (7,2) to (4,2). The opponent occupies three center squares: Green (3,3), Blue (3,4), and Blue (4,4). Green (5,3) can still move directly to (4,3) and complete center occupation immediately. Losses: Red 2, Yellow 1, opponent colors 0; no eliminations.

### Our plan
The move blocks Green (4,0) from reaching (4,3) and places Yellow beside the empty center. If the opponent does not complete the center, aim to land Yellow on (4,3), sandwiching Blue (4,4) against Yellow (4,5). Preserve Red, which remains one loss from elimination.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent prioritizes central occupation and aligned sandwich threats. Blue’s last move created an immediate three-square center majority.

### Lessons
Always test whether the next acting opponent color can fill the last center square; center victory is immediate and overrides longer tactical plans.
```

Green completes our four-square center occupation, securing the immediate win.
```memo
### Position read
We occupy all four central squares after Green moves to (4,3), completing center occupation for an immediate win.
### Our plan
The game is won by center occupation.
### Opponent tendencies
The opponent contested the center but could not disrupt the final route.
### Lessons
A supported two-turn center finish is decisive when the intervening opponent cannot occupy, capture, or block the last square.
```
